hook.line: The year journalist Kuroiwa Ruikō named the game “renju” — the start of its history as a sport.
hook.say: Hi! Let me guide you through the history of Gomoku.

ch.t: A game born on the Go board
ch.say: With a Go board and stones, anyone could play.
p: Its origin is unclear, but in Japan it is said to have long been enjoyed as an easy game for any Go board and stones.
After an international federation formed in 1988, strong players emerged in Russia, Estonia, Sweden, Taiwan and elsewhere.
st: Five in a row on the go board spreads among townsfolk
Kuroiwa Ruikō names it renju and organises it
Forbidden moves for Black balance the game
The RIF is founded in Stockholm
World championships; Russia and Estonia rise

ch.say: Its name and rules kept evolving.
tl: Five-in-a-row on a Go board is said to spread among townspeople
Kuroiwa Ruikō names it “renju” in his newspaper
Forbidden moves for Black only, to curb the first-move advantage
The Renju International Federation is founded in Stockholm
World championships begin, held every two years
Computers prove 15×15 gomoku a first-player win
Free renju (with forbidden moves) also shown a first-player win

ch.say: Black is too strong, so it gets a handicap!
ch.cap: Black playing on the □ makes a “double three” — forbidden
p: Moving first gives Black a huge edge, so renju forbids Black from making double threes, double fours and overlines (six or more).
Opening rules were added on top, in a long pursuit of fairness.
